proposals.title: Where your missed questions are: the gap to target, split by skill
proposals.what: A new full-width card #gap. On desktop it gets its own row right after next | mist; on a phone it comes second, after #next. Header: WHERE YOUR MISSED QUESTIONS ARE. Headline: 'On a 44-question section you miss about 17 now. 700 means missing about 7.' Below that, the top 6 skills are shown as rows, and 'Show all 19' expands the rest in place. Each row shows: the topic chip; '~2.1 of 3.1 questions missed a section'; a bar split into expected right and expected missed; 'could win back ~1.4'; '3 open mistakes'; 'last worked 12 days ago'; and a .btn 'Work on this · 10' (POST /api/drill {topics:[t], count:10, source:'today'}). A sort toggle offers 'Most questions first' (the default) and 'Quickest wins', which puts rows with open traps first. A named mistake closes in two clean answers. A skill with fewer than 5 answers gets an 'unmeasured' tag and uses its domain's mean. Helper line: 'Approximate. The SAT publishes domain shares, not skill shares, so a domain is split evenly across its skills.' Server: estimate.gap(learner). per_section(t) = 44 x domain share / topics in the domain, which gives Algebra 3.1, Advanced 5.1, PSDA 0.94 and Geo 1.65 per skill. p(t) = accuracy over the last 40 non-repeat answers, reweighted to module 1's 7/8/7 easy/medium/hard mix. missed = per_section x (1 - p). winback = max(0, missed - per_section x 0.15), that is, the gain from reaching Strong. allowed = 44 x (1 - frac), with frac from inverting scoring.ANCHORS. /api/today adds gap:{now_missed, allowed, rows:[{topic, domain, per_section, p, missed, winback, traps, answered, measured, last}]}. Up next's reason line quotes it: '~1.4 missed questions a section in these skills · 3 open mistakes'. The student works on the skills that hold the most missing questions, not the ones they like or the ones the week happened to bring. The target becomes a number they can count toward ('miss 7, not 17'), and every session starts with its value stated. Their score rises faster because the minutes go where the marginal points are.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Score Progress shows one number and a target, which read 0 until a full test and out of sync with their wizard. Their plan's 'Score gap: 1000 now, 1400 target' tile is a subtraction. Nothing they show says where the missing points are or which skill is worth the next hour. Their 'Why this task?' is free-text AI copy with no numbers.
proposals.needs: F4 estimate.py (R16) for the target and band; progress.board (mastery, answered, traps); BLUEPRINT and scoring.ANCHORS (both exist); S3 coach reason line. Plan (S7) could read the same rows for its slot allocation so the two never disagree.

proposals.title: I have N minutes: one tap builds the best session for the time you actually have
proposals.what: At the top of Up next there is a .choices row 'I have: 5 · 10 · 20 · 30 · 45 · 60 min'. It defaults to what is left of today's goal (at least 5), or 20 when no goal is set. Under it, a composition preview: a stacked bar plus one line per block, for example: '20 min · 13 questions: 2 check-ins due (Circles, Percentages) · 3 recalls · 3 mistake repairs · 5 new, mixed: Probability, Nonlinear functions'. Each block row has an x that removes it; its time goes back to 'new'. The pill reads 'Start · 20 min'. Seconds per question come from the learner's own median ms over their last 20 answers in each topic, clamped to 45-180 s, or 95 s without data. The server builds it with coach.compose(learner, minutes, tz), filling time in this order: check-ins due (R9, up to 30%); recalls due (see the recall proposal, up to 20%); open traps ordered by the gap ledger (up to 30%); new questions on the top two ledger skills, interleaved (the rest, at least 30%); and one keep-warm question on a Strong skill idle for 10 or more days, when 20 minutes or more are chosen. 5 min is labelled 'Streak saver' and holds only check-ins and traps. It is offered as the first choice after 18:00 local time when nothing has been done today. The drill body gains blocks:[{pool, ids|topics, count}] (F5 validates each block as a sub-body). POST /api/drill/preview {compose:minutes} returns the blocks. The session serves blocks in order, with new and redo mixed. When the budget runs out it offers 'Your 20 minutes are up · Finish · 5 more'. With an active plan, the blocks are today's plan tasks, trimmed to the minutes by dropping the lowest points-per-minute tasks first. The student starts every day in one tap, sized to the day, instead of skipping a day that can't fit the planned 60 minutes or picking comfortable topics. Every minute goes first to spaced retrieval and named-mistake repair, the cheapest points, then to interleaved new practice. That is the order the spacing and interleaving research supports, and it makes busy days count, so consistency rises.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep asks for daily time once, in the plan wizard (30 to 240 min chips), and their generator failed 3 of 3 times. Their dashboard offers their plan's checkbox tasks or a generic question of the day; nothing lets a student say 'I have 15 minutes' and get the best 15 minutes.
proposals.needs: F5 drill body 'blocks' and preview; R9 check-ins due; attempts.ms per topic; the gap ledger for ordering; S7 plan.today_summary tasks with minutes and value for the plan case; S4 session 'budget reached' footer.

proposals.title: Still got it? Spaced recall of everything you got right, with a 14-day due forecast
proposals.what: R9 brings back only fixed mistakes, at 3, 10 and 30 days. This extends spacing to every question type the student has solved. A clean first-try right answer on a template schedules a recall at +3 days. Each clean recall advances the stage (3, 10, 30, 60 days). A miss drops it to stage 0 (due tomorrow) and opens a trap as usual. Anything due after the exam is pulled to 5 days before it, as a last pass. Stored in a new table recall(learner, template, stage, due, last), updated in progress.record. progress.recall_due(learner, tz) returns [{template, topic, due, stage}] plus forecast[14]. Pool review gains due:true, which serves due templates on fresh seeds, oldest due first. On Today, the Review card (#mist, R30) changes its due line to 'Due today: 2 check-ins (fixed mistakes) · 6 recalls (types you had right)', with one .btn 'Do all 8 · 10 min'. Under that, a list of the due topics, each with a memory word: Fresh (inside its interval), Due, Fading (overdue by more than twice its interval). For example: 'Circles · right 3 of 3 · last seen 16 days ago · Fading'. The Today list gets a row 'Recall · 6 due · 7 min' that ticks itself when done. The calendar's future cells show '4 due' from the forecast, and the day detail lists them. The student spends 5 to 10 minutes a day answering new versions of question types they already solved, at growing intervals, instead of only practising what is new or broken. The testing effect and spacing keep a skill from week 1 alive on test day. Without it, 'Strong' skills decay silently and leak points in the section. The generator makes every recall a new question, so recalling never turns into remembering an answer.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has spaced repetition only for vocabulary ('Due Today N' in My Words, which stayed at 0 after grading). Their Math practice never brings back a solved type, and a fixed bank could only bring back the same question with the same answer.
proposals.needs: F4 recall table and progress.record hook; F5 pool 'review' with due; R9 check-ins, shown in the same row; F1 UI.calendar forecast marks; S10 Review's CHECK-INS DUE uses the same wording; the time-box proposal uses recalls as a block.

proposals.title: Pacing profile: speed against accuracy per skill, with speed sets and careful sets
proposals.what: A new card #pace: on desktop a full row after #study, with four quadrants side by side; on a phone after #mist. The headline projects a module: 'At your speed a 22-question module takes about 41 min. The clock is 35: about 4 questions would go blank or be rushed.' It is computed as the sum over skills of per_module(t) (half of the ledger's per_section) x the learner's median seconds, with unmeasured skills at 95 s. The four quadrants use each skill's last 30 days (5 or more non-repeat answers with ms): 'Banked' (median 95 s or less, 70% or more right); 'Speed up' (over 95 s, 70% or more right); 'Slow down' (60 s or less, under 70% right); 'Learn first' (over 95 s, under 70% right). Each lists its topic chips with the median, e.g. 'Systems 2:40'. Actions: 'Speed set · Systems · 10' sends POST /api/drill {topics:[t], count:10, timing:'custom', minutes: ceil(10 x max(80, median-20)/60)}, with the pace alert at that target. The summary then shows 'median 2:40 -> 1:58'. 'Careful set · Percentages · 8' is untimed. Before each question it shows the student's last fast wrong pick on that type ('Last time: 0:38, picked: added the percentages'). /api/today adds pace:{module_minutes, over_questions, rows:[{topic, median_ms, acc, n, quad}]} from progress.pace(learner), the same median function as Plan's slow-skill rule (median over 120 s times a skill). The student learns which skills cost them the clock and trains those under a shrinking per-question target. They also see which skills they rush and miss. SAT Math gives 35 minutes for 22 questions. A slow-but-right skill turns into blanks or rushed guesses at the end of a module, and a fast-wrong skill is slips. Both lose points with no content gap, and no amount of content study fixes them.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's report payload has no time per question at all. Their QBank stopwatch resets on reload. Their only time analysis is the contest 'average seconds per answered question, by difficulty', which was empty. Nothing on their dashboard mentions pace.
proposals.needs: attempts.ms (exists; tests via R7 qstate ms into record_paper); the gap ledger's per_section; S4 custom timing plus the per-question pace alert (in Practice spec); S7 sharing the median helper.

proposals.title: Test post-mortem: where the points went, split into causes, each with its own fix
proposals.what: On every finished test card on Today (and in the report hero, via S6's sitting card), the single 'Fix 13' becomes a split: '13 missed: 6 concept · 3 slips · 3 out of time · 1 grid-in entry', drawn as a stacked bar with a legend. Definitions, computed in /api/history rows as lost:{concept, slip, time, entry, blank}. Time: blanks when the module ended on the clock, plus wrong answers given in under 20 s in the module's last 5 minutes. Entry: a grid-in where the new scoring.entry_error(given, key) returns short_decimal (value within 0.01 of the key but too few digits: 0.66 for 2/3, which grid_equal already rejects), mixed_number ('1 1/2' equal to 3/2), too_long (more than 5 characters positive or 6 negative), or unit (a % or unit typed). Slip: wrong on a topic with 80% or more first-try right over its previous 20 answers (R9 kind 'slip'). Concept: every other wrong answer. Each part has its own .btn. Concept: 'Fix 6' (pool redo, from_session, only those qids). Slip: 'Careful set · 8' on those topics. Time: 'Pace set · 10' on the module's slowest topics. Entry: 'Grid-in entry · 5', grid-ins whose keys are fractions or repeating decimals, with the rule shown after each. A toggle 'Retest these in 2 days' writes retests(learner, session, due). On that day the Today list shows 'Retest Sep 21's misses · 13 fresh versions' (fresh seeds on the missed templates) and ticks itself when done. Test-to-test deltas per domain sit under the band: 'Algebra +3 right vs Sep 14'. After a test, the student treats the four causes differently: study the concept, slow down, pace, fix the entry format. They no longer 're-read all the explanations', which spends the hour on material they already know. The 2-day retest is spaced retrieval of exactly what the test exposed.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Recent Tests card is TOTAL SCORE, R&W, Math and Review. Their results list puts wrong and blank answers in one red chip, their report gauge counts blanks as wrong, and their payload has no time per question. They cannot tell a time loss from a content loss, and nothing is retested.
proposals.needs: S6 /api/history modules with wrong/blank (R26, R35) plus the lost split; R7 qstate ms and timestamps for tests; R9 slip kind; a new scoring.entry_error beside grid_equal; F5 pools; a retests table (F4); S6 sitting card renders the split everywhere.

proposals.title: Confidence tap and blind spots: know when to trust your first answer
proposals.what: Every answer hosted on Today gets an optional three-way tap before Check: 'Sure · Not sure · Guess' (K cycles it). That covers the day's questions, Try one now and the time-boxed set, and practice gets it through a pref 'confidence' (default on for Today, off elsewhere). It is stored as attempts.conf (sure|unsure|guess; guess also sets R8 guess=1). Rules in progress.record: sure-and-wrong opens the trap as kind 'blindspot' with owed 3. It sorts to the top of the Review card with the tag 'You were sure'. unsure-and-right opens owed 1, which is R9's existing 'unsure'. A calibration strip in the Review card, shown once 20 or more answers are tagged: 'Last 30 days · Sure: 86% right (58) · Not sure: 54% (24) · Guess: 30% (10)', with one reading line. Sure at 90% or more: 'Trust your sure answers on test day and spend the saved time on the not-sure ones.' 75-89%: 'Mostly reliable: re-check sure answers only on the last step.' Under 75%: 'You miss 1 in 4 answers you are sure of: re-read what the question asks before choosing.' The day's-questions crowd line adds 'People who were sure got it right 71%'. The student commits to a confidence before seeing the key and learns whether their 'sure' can be trusted. Their confidently wrong mistakes, which they would never review because they think they know them, get extra repair. On test day they spend flag-and-return time where it pays.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no confidence data anywhere. Their QOTD is a one-shot right or wrong, and QBank's unlimited retries make even their accuracy meaningless. Our Tests spec puts Sure/Unsure/Guess in the exam only, off by default. Today makes it the daily habit and the place where calibration is read.
proposals.needs: F3 UI.workspace confidence control in inline and practice modes (the exam control exists in the Tests spec); F4 attempts.conf column and the record() rule; R9 kind 'blindspot'; R11 prefs key 'confidence'; S3 crowd split by conf in daily.py.

proposals.title: Your mistake patterns: one habit across many skills, drilled across skills
proposals.what: The Review card (#mist) gets a segmented 'By mistake · By pattern' control. By pattern groups open and 30-day traps by norm (R8/R9; Review's norm-to-templates index already finds 79 misconceptions shared across templates). For example: 'Changed the sign of the slope · 5 times · in Linear functions, Two-variable data, Systems', with a .btn 'Pattern drill · 8'. That sends POST /api/drill {pool:'related', ids:norm, count:8}, which serves items across templates where one option names the misconception (via want), so resisting the trap is practised in every skill it lives in. Above the list is a 30-day cause line from R9 kinds: '11 concept · 6 slips · 2 grid-in entry · 3 blind spots'. Each count links to its drill: slips to a careful set, entry to the grid-in entry set, blind spots to redo with those ids. The student sees that four 'different' mistakes are one habit and fixes the habit once, not one topic at a time. Fixing a pattern closes points in every skill it appears in. A per-topic list hides that one error is costing points in several places.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's dashboard shows no mistakes at all. Their review modal's 'Distractor Analysis' is prose about one question, never added up, and their redo API has no UI. A bank without labelled distractors cannot group mistakes by cause.
proposals.needs: R8 attempts.norm; S10 norm index and pool 'related' (F5 want); R9 kinds; the blindspot kind from the confidence proposal.

proposals.title: Worked-example pairs for new and stuck skills: study one solved, then solve its twin
proposals.what: The coach flags a skill as new (under 3 answers) or stuck (mastery under 0.3 after 6 or more answers). When Up next's set contains such a skill, the set starts with two worked pairs for it. The reason line says so: 'New skill: Circles · starts with 2 worked examples'. Pair 1: a worked card showing the stem, the key marked, the rationale, and 'Traps on this type', with each wrong option's misconception (Item.reasons). One button, 'Got it · try one', follows, then the same template on a fresh seed to answer. Pair 2 fades the support: the next template shows only 'Traps to avoid' before the student answers, with no rationale. After that, plain practice. Inside any set, a .quiet 'Show me one solved' in the question strip puts a worked twin of the current question's template before it. The current question stays unanswered and still counts. Worked seeds are db.remember-ed so they are never served as questions, and worked cards file no attempt and do not move mastery. Drill cfg gains worked:n (F5). The workspace gains a read-only 'worked' mode (F3). With a new skill, the student studies a solved example with its traps named, then solves the twin. They don't guess through the first questions and pile up mistakes that then have to be un-learned. The worked-example effect is strongest for novices, and naming the traps first stops misconceptions from forming. Only a generator gives an exact, unlimited twin for every example.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep teaches nothing before asking. Explanations appear only after an answer, their QOTD never shows the key, and a fixed bank cannot make a twin of the example it just showed.
proposals.needs: F5 cfg 'worked' (serve n worked cards per flagged template, remembered, no attempt filed); F3 workspace 'worked' mode; S3 coach flags new/stuck and the reason line; S4 'Show me one solved' in the question strip.

proposals.title: Measure what we cannot see yet: an 8-question skill check for unmeasured skills
proposals.what: The gap card and the Score card both list unmeasured skills (under 5 answers): 'Unmeasured: Probability, Circles, Margin of error, Statistical claims · they hold about 5 questions a section · your band is wider because of them'. A .btn 'Measure them · 8 questions · 12 min' sends POST /api/drill {pool:'untried', topics:unmeasured, each:2, adaptive:true, source:'measure'}: two questions per skill, starting at medium, stepping up after a right answer and down after a miss (R33). On finishing, the summary and Today show each one move from unmeasured to a measured row in the ledger ('Circles: ~0.6 of 1.65 missed a section'). The coach stops using domain-size order for those skills. The estimate's confidence reason (R16) adds 'N skills unmeasured' and drops it once they are measured. In 12 minutes the student gives the coach data on the skills it is guessing about. The next week's practice then targets real leaks. A never-tried skill can be the biggest leak, and priorities are only as good as the measurement behind them.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's plan wizard makes the student self-rate each domain Focus, Normal or Strong. Their estimate drops floor-score sections, and nothing measures skill by skill, so their plan's priorities rest on a guess.
proposals.needs: progress.board answered per topic; F5 pool untried with each and adaptive; the gap ledger; F4 estimate.py confidence reason.

proposals.title: Readiness for test day, and a taper in the final two weeks
proposals.what: The SAT countdown card (#exam) gains a READINESS list headed '3 of 6 ready'. Each row is computed and, when unmet, has its own action: 'Every skill practised: 17 of 19' (links to the 8-question measure); 'Timed full sections in the last 6 weeks: 1 of 3' (Start section); 'Pace: your median 1:52 a question, SAT pace 1:35' (Pace set); 'Open mistakes in big skills: 5' (Fix); 'Check-ins and recalls due: 8' (Do all); 'Grid-in entry errors this month: 2' (Grid-in entry). Without a plan, Up next switches to taper order in the last 14 days: timed mixed sets at the module difficulty mix, check-ins and recalls, and a one-time 'Last pass' drill over every mistake fixed since the student began (fresh seeds). There are no new skills in the last 3 days. The eve reads '15 minutes: your 5 most-missed mistakes, one each, then stop.' Exam day shows only the checklist. With a plan, Plan's Final phase (S7) drives Up next and the readiness list only reports. The student sees what 'ready' means in concrete terms and closes the unmet items. The last two weeks go to consolidation, timing and relapse checks instead of cramming new material. Full timed sittings build pacing and stamina, and the last pass catches fixed mistakes that have come back.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's countdown is a DD:HH:MM:SS clock with a date select that still offers past dates. It never says whether the student is ready or what the remaining days should hold.
proposals.needs: the pace, measure and recall proposals; R9 check-ins; F4 estimate sittings count; S7 Final phase (Plan owns the taper for plan users, and Today must not contradict it); S3 coach taper branch.

proposals.title: What your time bought: progress stated in questions, not minutes
proposals.what: The Study card (#study) gains a section 'WHAT YOUR TIME BOUGHT' with a This week | This month toggle. One row per skill worked: 'Percentages · 1h 10m · 41% -> 78% right · ~+1.2 questions a section · 3 mistakes closed', sorted by gain. Mastery before comes from mastery_of over the attempts before the period, the same as the week recap's 'before'. Questions a section come from the gap ledger. A totals line: 'This month: 6h 20m · ~+3.5 questions a section · 14 mistakes closed'. A 'Comfort time' line appears when over 30% of the period's minutes went to skills already Strong at the time: 'Comfort time: 35% of this week went to skills you already have', with 'Put it on Probability instead' (a set on the top ledger skill). After each finished session, Up next shows one line: 'Last set: Circles 6/8 · 38% -> 52% · 1 mistake closed'. A consistency figure sits next to the streak: '5 of the last 7 study days met your goal', and a broken streak does not zero it. Once today's goal is met, a .quiet 'Tomorrow at 17:00 · 30 min? Add to calendar' offers a single .ics event with an alarm (UI.ics(event)), a time and a length the student commits to. The student sees which hours moved their score and which were comfort, and moves the comfort time to weak skills. They come back because progress shows in the unit that matters. Consistency and a stated time for tomorrow keep daily practice going better than a streak that resets.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep shows study minutes today and this month, and a streak pill that disagrees with the profile. Their achievements are four hard-coded tiles with a dead 'View All'. Minutes alone say nothing about whether the practice worked.
proposals.needs: F4 progress.days minutes per topic (attempt ms); mastery_of at a date (as the spec's week.moved); the gap ledger's per_section; F1 UI.ics(event); S7 plan streak rules for rest days (R13).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Date eyebrow, time-of-day greeting with the name, and four chips: study streak, minutes today, SAT in N days, plan progress.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The greeting and date are theirs. The chips repeat numbers that the cards below already show, so the student has nothing new to act on.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A 'Since last time' line built from what changed since the student's previous visit (last visit stored server-side): 'Since Monday: 6 mistakes closed · Circles reached Strong · estimate 520-600 -> 540-620 · 8 due today'. Each part links to its card, so coming back opens with evidence of progress and today's first job.

parity_gaps.feature: Questions of the day (two, the same for everyone, Check step, one try, streak)
parity_gaps.spec_says: An MC and a grid-in, confirm then Check, the key shown, the misconception and crowd % per option, 5 more like this, Harder, past days, a streak.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: They also have two daily questions, a Check step, one attempt and a streak pill. Ours explains more, but the question is still a random daily item with no tie to the student, and it is forgotten tomorrow.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Put it into the learning loop. A wrong answer automatically schedules a check-in on that template in 3 days, and the past-days strip shows 'Back on Sat'. Add the confidence tap before Check, and split the crowd line by it ('people who were sure got it right 71%'). Add a third personal slot, 'Yours', a due recall, that counts for the day's-questions streak.

parity_gaps.feature: Grid-in rules on the day's grid-in
parity_gaps.spec_says: A Grid-in rules popover: 5 or 6 characters, fractions or decimals, no mixed numbers.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their SPR items also show the directions and an answer preview. A popover the student has to open does not stop the points leaking.
parity_gaps.upgrade: After Check, classify entry errors with scoring.entry_error: 'Right value, wrong entry: the SAT marks 0.66 wrong for 2/3. Enter .666, .667 or 2/3.' Mixed numbers, short decimals and typed units get the same treatment. File them as kind 'entry', count them on the Review card and in the readiness list, and offer 'Grid-in entry · 5'. grid_equal already applies College Board's rule, so detecting these is cheap.

parity_gaps.feature: Study time today and this month
parity_gaps.spec_says: Four figures (today, week, month, active days), goal bars, and minutes counted from attempts and sittings in the local zone.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs shows STUDY TIME TODAY and THIS MONTH. Adding a week and active days is still only a measure of effort.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Split the minutes by what they bought, as a stacked bar: recall and check-ins, repairs, new practice, tests, and comfort (skills already Strong). Warn when comfort goes over 30%, and add the 'What your time bought' gains in questions a section.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Heat from minutes relative to the goal, plan marks, the exam mark, and a day detail with minutes, questions, accuracy and sittings.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs is a month calendar that marks active days. Ours adds heat and a working detail panel, but it still only looks backwards.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Make it look forward as well. Future cells show the check-ins and recalls falling due (a 14-day forecast from R9 plus recall) and the plan's tests. A past day's detail lists what moved that day ('Circles +0.08 · 2 mistakes closed'), not only the sittings.

parity_gaps.feature: Live SAT countdown and date picker
parity_gaps.spec_says: DD:HH:MM:SS to 8:00 AM, upcoming official dates, a custom date, the plan line, and a checklist in the last 7 days.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs is the same ticking clock above a date select. Seconds ticking do nothing for a score, and a checklist of logistics is not readiness.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Lead with the study budget: '10 days · 7 study days · ~5h 15m at your goal · 1 test left'. Show the seconds small. Add the computed readiness list with an action on each unmet row, and the final-two-weeks taper for students without a plan.

parity_gaps.feature: Score card: band, target, gap and pace
parity_gaps.spec_says: The band, the SAT total from an optional R&W score, a scale bar, '+140 to target · about 20 a week', drift, an 8-point trend, and domain rows.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: '+140 to target · about 20 a week' is their wizard's 'about 60 points per week' moved to Today. Theirs shows a current score and a target too. Neither says where the points are or whether the pace is on track.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Show the gap in questions a section, with the per-skill ledger ('miss 7, not 17'). With 3 or more scored sittings, add a projected exam-day range from the slope of the student's own estimate midpoints over the last 30 days, worded plainly: 'On your current trend: 580-640 by Oct 3 · behind your target by ~3 questions a section.'

parity_gaps.spec_says: A Math target as a number and a slider with quick choices, optional R&W now and target, Save disabled until something changes, one shared field.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs is a number input with a 400-1600 bar and Save disabled until you type. Ours has the same shape with more fields.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Live feasibility while dragging: '700 = miss about 7 of 44. You miss about 17 now. Your last 4 weeks: ~+1 question a section a week, so ~600-640 by Oct 3.' Show a ledger preview of where the 10 questions would come from ('Nonlinear functions 3 · Percentages 2 · ...'). The target then comes with a concrete route, and an unrealistic target is flagged honestly.

parity_gaps.feature: Today list (the plan's tasks for today) and Up next's reason
parity_gaps.spec_says: Rows that tick themselves, with progress, a one-line Why, Skip / Undo skip and Move; N of M done; minutes left; All done.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: This matches their Today's Plan card (N of M, min left, All Done, Full Plan, Why this task?, Skip, Move). The Why lines are fixed strings ('Your weakest skills right now'), where theirs is free-text AI copy.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Each Why states its value from the ledger: '~1.4 questions a section · 3 open mistakes · last worked 12 days ago'. Add a 'Short on time?' control that resizes today's list to N minutes and keeps the tasks with the most points per minute. That beats skipping whole tasks, and beats their move-only reschedule.

parity_gaps.feature: Plan card: stat row, week pager, behind line, drift
parity_gaps.spec_says: Day 12 of 45, % done, days to the SAT, +140 to target; a week strip with done, partial, missed and skipped; a behind line with Change daily time; the drift prompt.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: These are their four stat tiles (days to exam, streak, plan complete %, score gap), their '3 / 7' week pager and their behind and drift banners, one for one.
parity_gaps.upgrade: State the week's goals as outcomes, not task counts: 'This week: close 6 mistakes (4) · Circles to Strong (62% -> 70%) · 1 timed section (0)'. When behind, show what a shorter day would drop: 'At 30 min a day the plan keeps the fixes and check-ins and drops 2 new-skill sets' (lowest points per minute first). The student then knows the cost of each choice.

parity_gaps.spec_says: The band, a route tag, right/asked, a mini scale, missed-question chips (wrong vs blank), Review, Fix N and New one like this.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs shows the score and Review. Our chips and Fix bring the report one tap closer, but the card still treats every lost point the same way.
parity_gaps.upgrade: The lost-points split (concept, slips, out of time, grid-in entry, blank), each with its own fix. A 'Retest in 2 days' toggle that puts fresh versions of the misses on the Today list on that day. Per-domain deltas against the previous test.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Three labelled streaks from single sources, with the best streak, consistent across pages; rest days don't break the study streak (R13).
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: A streak pill is their mechanic. Three of them is more of the same number, and a streak that resets to zero after one missed day is the moment students quit.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Put a consistency figure next to the streak ('5 of the last 7 study days met your goal') that a broken streak cannot wipe out. Offer the 5-minute 'Streak saver' (check-ins and traps only) after 18:00 local time when nothing is done. After the goal is met, ask 'Tomorrow at 17:00 · 30 min?' and add it to the calendar, a commitment that raises follow-through.

parity_gaps.spec_says: The four steps as links, a preview from the student's data, three bullets, 'Free, as many as you like', Build my plan.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their CTA's shape (eyebrow, title, three bullets, one button). The preview helps, but building still means going through a four-step wizard.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A one-tap plan: 'Start from 540 -> 620 · Oct 3 · 35 min on the 5 days you actually studied · focus: Nonlinear functions, Percentages', with every value prefilled from the estimate, the gap ledger, the next official date and the student's 14-day average minutes and weekdays. 'Use this plan' builds it at once, and 'Change' opens the wizard at step 1.
